headline: Why Does My Toilet Keep Clogging?
articleBody: It's super annoying when your toilet seems to clog all the time, right? There are usually a few key reasons why this happens, and understanding them can help you prevent future headaches. Often, it's about what's going down the drain – things like excessive toilet paper, wet wipes (even the 'flushable' ones!), cotton balls, or other foreign objects are big no-nos. Your toilet is designed to handle waste and toilet paper only. Another common culprit is an old, low-flush toilet. Older models might not have the flushing power needed to move waste efficiently through your pipes, making them more prone to blockages. Sometimes, a partial clog might be building up deeper in your drain line, possibly caused by tree roots or accumulated sludge, leading to frequent backups even with normal use. A worn-out or damaged flush valve assembly can also contribute by not creating enough water pressure for a good flush. While some minor clogs can be tackled with a plunger, if it's a recurring issue, it often means there's a more serious problem. That's when it's really time to call in the pros.
